note: Songs and stories at the Willow Bend fire at night (src/ai/camp.gd sing_along): companions sit round, one leads, the others join the refrain. Lyrics and stories are original, in period style. Each entry: who must be in camp, the lines in order (speaker per line).

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Oh, the Sable runs brown and the Sable runs slow, and it took my last dollar a long time ago.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: I gave it my boots and I gave it my mare, and it gave me a sandbar and left me there.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: So roll on, Sable, roll on by. There's nothing you owe me, and nothing owe I.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: I courted a widow in Port Linden town. She married a banker and burned my coat down.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: So roll on, Sable, roll on by. There's nothing you owe me, and nothing owe I.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: There's a lamp in a window of a house that I knew, and it burns every evening though nobody's due.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: It burns for the riders, it burns for the dead, it burns for the fool who rode off instead.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: So I'll ride past that window and I'll lift up my hat, for the light that's left burning. There's no more than that.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: In seventy-nine I sold a mule in Mesquite Wells that could count. Stamped a hoof for every dollar.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: To four. Unhappily, I had told the buyer he could count to ten.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: That ain't a story. That's a confession.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: My first winter with the county we found a rider froze in the saddle at Kestrel Pass. Horse still standing under him.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Letter in his coat, addressed to nobody. Just: To whoever finds me, the coffee is in the left bag.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: It was. Best coffee I ever drank. I think of him every time I make it.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Nobody else up? Then you'll get the short version. Once there was a cook who was never thanked. The end.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Roll on, Sable. Roll on by.
